summary: Offer Wadham Island light in the Wadham Islands off Newfoundland's northeast coast: brick tower in permanent use from 1858, de-staffed 1961, now a steel skeleton light shown seasonally.

light.note: Coast Guard list (modified 2026-06-23): Fl W 5s, seasonal. LHF and Rowlett: white flash every 3 s. History: fixed white (1858), white flash every 30 s (1890), occulting (1919).

structures.material: brick, encased in iron 1893 and in concrete 1961
structures.note: Original brick tower. LHF has it completed by 1 October 1857; Greenspond and Rowlett give 1858. Rowlett gives 12 m (40 ft) with a question mark.
Current light on a square skeleton tower with a red and white rectangular daymark (Coast Guard list: 7.1 m; Rowlett: 7 m). Build date is not given in these sources.
Keepers' dwelling with a pitched roof, given a mansard roof in 1886. Torn down in the 1990s for safety reasons (LHF).

staffing.note: After the 1961 concrete encasing the station was de-staffed; a former keeper was employed as caretaker (LHF).

access.note: Accessible only by private boat or helicopter (Greenspond). Site open, tower closed. Best seen by boat or from the air (LHF).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (site manager; LHF; Greenspond)

events.note: Red brick tower and attached wooden dwelling found complete on 1 October 1857 (LHF). Greenspond and Rowlett give 1858.
Strong gales delayed Inspector Oke's departure from St. John's in late September 1857 (LHF).
Fixed white light, double Argand burner, fourth-order lens, placed in permanent operation 4 October 1858 (LHF). The apparatus was installed in August 1858.
Charles Prowse placed in charge after complaints of 1862-63; keeper Thomas Hennessey and his son, an assistant, dismissed (LHF).
Tower coated inside and out with Portland cement (LHF). Rowlett: encased in cement in 1863.
Tower found in an extremely defective condition; new brickwork in cement; cast-iron gallery replaces the stone cornice (LHF).
Assistant keeper Henry Waterman came to an untimely end in the spring of 1880 by falling through the ice, per Inspector Nevill as quoted by LHF.
Pitched roof of the keepers' dwelling replaced with a mansard roof (LHF).
Fixed white changed to a white flash every thirty seconds, with a six-sided fourth-order lens (LHF).
Brick tower encased in iron (LHF; Rowlett).
Changed to occulting: visible five seconds, eclipsed five seconds (LHF).
Iron tower encased in reinforced concrete, octagonal in shape (LHF; Rowlett; Greenspond).
Station de-staffed; former keeper Walter Hicks employed as caretaker (LHF).

corrections.proposed: The 1858 brick tower is about 12 m (40 ft), lantern removed, inactive and still standing. The 7.1 m steel skeleton tower is the current light (no build date given).
corrections.why: The record puts the 1858 date and the 7.1 m height on one structure. The 7.1 m height belongs to the current steel skeleton tower (Coast Guard list); the original brick tower still stands (LHF; Rowlett).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Coast Guard list (modified 2026-06-23) lists the current light as seasonal; LHF says it shows today; Rowlett and Greenspond describe the old brick tower as inactive. Both are consistent: the old tower is inactive and the current light is listed as shown seasonally.

Not settled. The Coast Guard list gives Fl W 5s; LHF and Rowlett give a white flash every three seconds. The sources do not say when the characteristic changed. The Coast Guard list is the most recent official entry and is recorded.

LHF has the tower complete on 1 October 1857 and the light in permanent operation on 4 October 1858. Greenspond and Rowlett give 1858 for the tower. The record keeps 1858 as the lit date and notes the 1857 completion.
LHF gives 1863 as the start of Prowse's keepership and Greenspond gives 1862. LHF's account says he was sent in November 1862 and again in May 1863, and was placed in charge after that.

notes_for_editor: Nearly every fact from 1841 to 1961 comes from LighthouseFriends, which takes its quotations from the Newfoundland House of Assembly journals and from Inspectors' reports (Oke, Nevill) without page numbers. Those were not read; the quotations are as LHF gives them, with its transcription faults. The 1856 act is quoted only for the words LHF prints cleanly; LHF's text reads 'can he provided' there, so the story paraphrases that clause. The 1841 petition, the 1844 committee evidence and the 1880 Waterman death are LHF's account. The book LHF and Wikipedia cite for the island, Roland W. Abbott, The Million Dollar Rock (1994), was not available and is not cited. The corpus has no Newfoundland reports (the Canadian Marine series starts in 1900 and covers Canada), so no primary check was possible. Wikipedia's lead gives an 1852 'Spring of the Wadhams' sealing disaster and a Prowse keepership to 1901 (its own table gives 1899); neither is cited. The record's structure entry mixes the 1858 brick tower and the 7.1 m skeleton tower; corrected above. The Rowlett Newfoundland page gives the old tower's encasement dates, which match LHF's. Post-1960 names (Hicks) appear with years and roles only, as the sources give them. Fact-check of 2026-10-28: the 'extremely defective' and 'remains standing nearby' wording and several LHF sentences were rewritten in the story (LHF is a copyrighted source). Greenspond says 'accessible only by boat' in one line and 'private boat or helicopter' in another; the story uses the second. Greenspond and Rowlett both give the active light's tower as steel and the Coast Guard gives 7.1 m, while Greenspond gives 6 m and Rowlett 7 m; the story gives only the Coast Guard figure. Rowlett writes 'Inactive since early 1990s (?)'; the question mark is now stated in the story. Stephen Abbot is spelled as LHF spells it, with Greenspond's spelling noted. No Newfoundland primary report was available, so the 1841 petition, the 1844 committee, the 1856 act and the Oke and Nevill reports are checked only against LHF's transcription. Walter Hicks (caretaker from 1961) is named only as the sources give him, with his role.
